findings.rationale: The materialized filename is derived only from the source stem and process ID, and std::fs::write does not create it exclusively. Concurrent or reentrant materializations of the same source within one process therefore share a path: one call can overwrite another's file and either guard can delete it while still in use. A pre-existing path is also overwritten and subsequently removed.

PROJECT_BLOCKS and the documented raw-block contract include evaluator and failure_mode, but RAW_BLOCKS omits both. parse_ai_project consequently recognizes their boundaries and then silently discards them through the default match arm instead of preserving the promised AiRawBlock entries.

The project parser accepts arbitrary whitespace between a declaration kind and name, while is_ai_project requires a literal space on one line. Parser-valid declarations using a tab or newline can therefore bypass the AI-project checking path and be routed to an incompatible frontend.
